Titanium Implant: Metal Artifacts

Define a metal yourself, put it in a water phantom, and measure the artifacts it leaves in the standard reconstruction chain.

No metal ships in the built-in material table, and that is the point: any implant is one XA.Material call, an elemental composition and a density, with NIST XCOM (through XrayAttenuation.jl) supplying its cross-sections. Two 1.5 cm titanium rods in a 26 cm water cylinder are scanned beside an identical cylinder whose rods are water, so their difference is the artifact alone.

Metal artifacts come from two physical mechanisms that BasisSimulator.jl models by construction:

  1. Beam hardening. The polychromatic forward model sums $I = \sum_E w_E\, e^{-L_E}$ before the log, so a dense high-$Z$ object hardens the transmitted spectrum and the line integrals stop growing in proportion to the path length. Reconstructed: dark bands, most of all between two metal objects.

  2. Photon starvation. Behind thick metal few photons reach the detector, so quantum and electronic noise dominate those rays. Reconstructed: noisy streaks along the directions that cross the metal.

The reconstruction is the package's standard chain, a water beam-hardening correction and FDK. The package ships no metal-artifact-reduction (MAR) algorithm, and the water correction is not designed for metal; the notebook measures how much artifact is left.

import BasisSimulator as BS
begin
    import CUDA
    # the NVIDIA GPU's array type, or Array on a host without one (on Apple silicon, Metal.MtlArray)
    AT = CUDA.functional() ? CUDA.CuArray : Array
    to_gpu(x) = AT(x)
    GPU_BACKEND = (name = string(nameof(AT)),)
end;

"""A blank drawing area at `position`: equal scales, no axes, limits `(x0, x1, y0, y1)`."""
function canvas(position, limits; background = COLORS.paper)
    ax = Mke.Axis(position; aspect = Mke.DataAspect(), backgroundcolor = background)
    Mke.hidedecorations!(ax)
    Mke.hidespines!(ax)
    Mke.limits!(ax, limits...)
    return ax
end;
"""The corners of a rectangle centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, its corners rounded by `r`."""
function rounded_rect(c, w, h, r)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = c[1] - w / 2, c[2] - h / 2, c[1] + w / 2, c[2] + h / 2
    r = min(r, w / 2, h / 2)
    arc(cx, cy, θ0) = [
        Mke.Point2f(cx + r * cos(θ), cy + r * sin(θ))
        for θ in range(θ0, θ0 + π / 2; length = 8)
    ]
    return vcat(
        arc(x1 - r, y0 + r, -π / 2),
        arc(x1 - r, y1 - r, 0.0),
        arc(x0 + r, y1 - r, π / 2),
        arc(x0 + r, y0 + r, π),
    )
end;
"""A straight arrow from `a` to `b`; `head` is the arrowhead's size in pixels."""
function arrow!(
    ax,
    a,
    b;
    color = COLORS.muted,
    linewidth = 2.5,
    head = 15,
    linestyle = :solid,
)
    a, b = Mke.Point2f(a), Mke.Point2f(b)
    Mke.lines!(ax, [a, b]; color, linewidth, linestyle)
    t = b - a
    Mke.scatter!(
        ax,
        [b];
        marker = :utriangle,
        markersize = head,
        rotation = atan(t[2], t[1]) - π / 2,
        color,
        markerspace = :pixel,
    )
    return nothing
end;
"""
A box in a flow chart: centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, a bold `title` and an optional smaller
`subtitle`. `accent` colours its outline (and a strip down its left edge).
"""
function node!(
    ax,
    c,
    title;
    subtitle = "",
    w = 3.0,
    h = 1.0,
    accent = COLORS.violet,
    fill = COLORS.card,
    textcolor = COLORS.ink,
    subcolor = COLORS.muted,
    titlesize = 19,
    subtitlesize = 15,
    code = false,
)
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        rounded_rect(c, w, h, 0.14);
        color = fill,
        strokecolor = accent,
        strokewidth = 2,
    )
    strip = rounded_rect((c[1] - w / 2 + 0.06, c[2]), 0.12, h - 0.1, 0.05)
    Mke.poly!(ax, strip; color = accent)
    font = code ? "DejaVu Sans Mono Bold" : :bold
    dy = isempty(subtitle) ? 0.0 : 0.17 * h
    Mke.text!(
        ax,
        c[1] + 0.05,
        c[2] + dy;
        text = title,
        align = (:center, :center),
        fontsize = titlesize,
        font,
        color = textcolor,
    )
    isempty(subtitle) ||
        Mke.text!(
            ax,
            c[1] + 0.05,
            c[2] - 0.22 * h;
            text = subtitle,
            align = (:center, :center),
            fontsize = subtitlesize,
            color = subcolor,
        )
    return nothing
end;
"""
A flow chart: `nodes` maps a key to `(x, y, title, subtitle, accent)` (subtitle and accent
optional), `edges` lists `from => to` pairs, drawn as arrows between the boxes' edges, and
`labels` (optional) puts a note on an edge. Returns the canvas.
"""
function flow_chart!(position, nodes, edges; limits, w = 3.0, h = 1.0, labels = Dict())
    ax = canvas(position, limits)
    box(key) = nodes[key]
    function port(from, to)
        a, b = box(from), box(to)
        if abs(b[2] - a[2]) < 1.0e-6
            # side by side
            s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
            return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
        elseif abs(b[1] - a[1]) < 1.0e-6
            # one above the other
            s = sign(b[2] - a[2])
            return (a[1], a[2] + s * h / 2), (b[1], b[2] - s * h / 2)
        else
            # leave sideways, arrive on the facing side
            s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
            return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
        end
    end
    for (from, to) in edges
        p, q = port(from, to)
        if abs(p[1] - q[1]) < 1.0e-6 || abs(p[2] - q[2]) < 1.0e-6
            # straight across or straight down
            arrow!(ax, p, q)
        else
            # a right-angled connector: across to the gap's middle, along it, then in
            mx = (p[1] + q[1]) / 2
            Mke.lines!(
                ax,
                Mke.Point2f[p, (mx, p[2]), (mx, q[2])];
                color = COLORS.muted,
                linewidth = 2.5,
            )
            arrow!(ax, (mx, q[2]), q)
        end
        haskey(labels, from => to) &&
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                (p[1] + q[1]) / 2,
                q[2] + 0.12;
                text = labels[from => to],
                align = (:center, :bottom),
                fontsize = 15,
                color = COLORS.muted,
            )
    end
    for (_, n) in nodes
        node!(
            ax,
            (n[1], n[2]),
            n[3];
            subtitle = length(n) >= 4 ? n[4] : "",
            accent = length(n) >= 5 ? n[5] : COLORS.violet,
            w,
            h,
        )
    end
    return ax
end;
"""
A CT gantry seen along z, centred at the origin: the source(s) at radius `sid` (one per entry
of `angles`, degrees), the fan, the detector arc at `sdd` from each source, and a round object
of radius `r_object`. Draws on `ax` in the colours of `dark` (the locator band) or paper.
"""
function gantry!(
    ax;
    sid = 5.4,
    sdd = 9.5,
    angles = (90.0,),
    fan_deg = 50.0,
    r_object = 2.0,
    detector_colors = (COLORS.cyan,),
    labels = ("Tube",),
    dark = true,
    object = true,
)
    ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
    ring = dark ? COLORS.night_card : COLORS.card
    Mke.poly!(ax, Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid + 0.9); color = ring)
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid - 1.6);
        color = dark ? COLORS.night : COLORS.paper,
    )
    for (k, θ) in enumerate(angles)
        θ = deg2rad(θ)
        s = Mke.Point2f(sid * cos(θ), sid * sin(θ))
        half = deg2rad(fan_deg / 2)
        # the fan, from the focal spot to the detector arc (a circle about the source)
        edge = Mke.Point2f[
            s + sdd * Mke.Point2f(cos(θ + π + φ), sin(θ + π + φ))
            for φ in range(-half, half; length = 40)
        ]
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            Mke.Point2f.(vcat([s], edge));
            color = (COLORS.beam, 0.22),
            strokewidth = 0,
        )
        Mke.lines!(ax, edge; color = detector_colors[mod1(k, end)], linewidth = 9)
        Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :rect, markersize = 26, color = ink)
        Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :circle, markersize = 9, color = COLORS.beam)
        Mke.text!(
            ax,
            s * 1.18;
            text = labels[mod1(k, end)],
            align = (:center, :center),
            fontsize = 17,
            font = :bold,
            color = ink,
        )
    end
    object &&
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), r_object);
            color = (COLORS.blue, 0.55),
            strokecolor = ink,
            strokewidth = 1.5,
        )
    return ax
end;
"""
The dark locator band that opens a notebook: `n` panels side by side, each a canvas with
`limits`, its `titles[i]` and `subtitles[i]` underneath. Returns the figure and the canvases;
draw into them, then show the figure.
"""
function locator_band(titles, subtitles; limits, size = (1500, 560))
    fig = Mke.Figure(;
        size,
        backgroundcolor = COLORS.night,
        figure_padding = (10, 10, 18, 10),
    )
    axes = [
        canvas(fig[1, i], limits[i]; background = COLORS.night)
        for i in eachindex(titles)
    ]
    for i in eachindex(titles)
        Mke.Label(
            fig[2, i],
            titles[i];
            fontsize = 25,
            font = :bold,
            color = COLORS.night_ink,
            tellwidth = false,
        )
        Mke.Label(
            fig[3, i],
            subtitles[i];
            fontsize = 17,
            color = COLORS.night_muted,
            tellwidth = false,
        )
    end
    Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 1, 8)
    Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 2, 2)
    return fig, axes
end;

The colour titanium is drawn in: a steel grey.

"""The colour titanium is drawn in: a steel grey."""
const METAL = Mke.RGBf(0.45, 0.47, 0.5)
draw_rods!

The phantom mask slice (0 air, 1 water, 2 rod) drawn on ax in cm, centred, vox cm per voxel, air left clear; rod colours the rods, alpha the water.

"""
The phantom `mask` slice (0 air, 1 water, 2 rod) drawn on `ax` in cm, centred, `vox` cm per
voxel, air left clear; `rod` colours the rods, `alpha` the water.
"""
function draw_rods!(ax, mask, vox; rod = METAL, alpha = 0.45)
    n1, n2 = size(mask)
    colours = Dict(
        0 => Mke.RGBAf(0, 0, 0, 0),
        1 => Mke.RGBAf(COLORS.blue.r, COLORS.blue.g, COLORS.blue.b, alpha),
        2 => Mke.RGBAf(rod),
    )
    Mke.image!(
        ax,
        (-n1 / 2 * vox, n1 / 2 * vox),
        (-n2 / 2 * vox, n2 / 2 * vox),
        [colours[Int(m)] for m in mask];
        interpolate = false,
    )
    return ax
end
pixel_rect

The rectangle (cm) that pixels is × js cover on an n-pixel grid of dx cm pixels, centred.

"""The rectangle (cm) that pixels `is × js` cover on an `n`-pixel grid of `dx` cm pixels, centred."""
function pixel_rect(is, js, n, dx)
    x0 = (first(is) - 0.5 - (n + 1) / 2) * dx
    y0 = (first(js) - 0.5 - (n + 1) / 2) * dx
    return Mke.Rect2f(x0, y0, length(is) * dx, length(js) * dx)
end
inside_water

Which pixels of an n-pixel grid of dx cm pixels lie inside the 26 cm water cylinder.

"""Which pixels of an `n`-pixel grid of `dx` cm pixels lie inside the 26 cm water cylinder."""
inside_water(n, dx) = [
    hypot((i - (n + 1) / 2) * dx, (j - (n + 1) / 2) * dx) <= 13.0
    for i in 1:n, j in 1:n
]
dimension!

A dimension line from a to b, arrowheads at both ends, text beside its middle.

"""A dimension line from `a` to `b`, arrowheads at both ends, `text` beside its middle."""
function dimension!(
    ax,
    a,
    b,
    text;
    align = (:center, :bottom),
    offset = (0, 6),
    fontsize = 16,
)
    m = (Mke.Point2f(a) + Mke.Point2f(b)) / 2
    arrow!(ax, m, a; linewidth = 1.8, head = 11)
    arrow!(ax, m, b; linewidth = 1.8, head = 11)
    Mke.text!(ax, m; text, align, offset, fontsize, color = COLORS.ink)
    return nothing
end

1. Titanium as a Custom XA.Material

Titanium is exposed by XrayAttenuation.jl as an Element, not a prebuilt Material, so we construct the material ourselves: pure Ti ($Z = 22$, mass fraction 1.0) at 4.54 g/cm³. ZA_ratio and the mean excitation energy I come from the element data (0.45948, 233 eV).

titanium = BS.XA.Material(
    "Titanium (implant)",
    0.45948,         # ⟨Z/A⟩ for Ti
    233.0u"eV",      # mean excitation energy
    4.54u"g/cm^3",   # bulk density
    Dict(22 => 1.0), # elemental composition: pure Ti
);

Why titanium hardens the beam: 1.5 cm of water lets most photons of a 120 kVp spectrum through at every energy, but 1.5 cm of titanium stops nearly all of them below about 50 keV. What crosses a rod is a much harder spectrum, and a water correction maps its line integrals as if it were not.

2. The Phantom: Water Cylinder and Two Titanium Rods

A 26 cm water cylinder with two 1.5 cm titanium rods, 4 cm either side of the centre (two rods, so that the classic between-rod dark band appears). A second phantom is the same cylinder with the rods made of water: scanned identically, it is the artifact-free reference every measurement below is compared with.

phantom_mask = let
    n = 128
    nz = 8
    vox = 30.0 / n # 30 cm field, cm per voxel
    mask = zeros(UInt8, n, n, nz)
    c = (n + 1) / 2
    r_water = 13.0 / vox # 26 cm diameter water cylinder
    r_ti = 0.75 / vox    # 1.5 cm diameter rods
    rods = ((c - 4.0 / vox, c), (c + 4.0 / vox, c))
    for k in 1:nz, j in 1:n, i in 1:n
        (i - c)^2 + (j - c)^2 <= r_water^2 || continue
        mask[i, j, k] = any((i - x)^2 + (j - y)^2 <= r_ti^2 for (x, y) in rods) ? 2 : 1
    end
    (mask = mask, vox = vox)
end;
phantom = BS.Phantom(
    to_gpu(phantom_mask.mask),
    Dict(0 => BS.XA.Materials.air, 1 => BS.XA.Materials.water, 2 => titanium),
    ntuple(_ -> phantom_mask.vox, 3),
);
phantom_reference = BS.Phantom( # the same geometry, rods made of water
    to_gpu(phantom_mask.mask),
    Dict(0 => BS.XA.Materials.air, 1 => BS.XA.Materials.water, 2 => BS.XA.Materials.water),
    ntuple(_ -> phantom_mask.vox, 3),
);
blend_water

The reference phantom's rods: water, the colour draw_rods! gives water, without transparency.

"""The reference phantom's rods: water, the colour `draw_rods!` gives water, without transparency."""
blend_water() = Mke.RGBf(
    0.45 * COLORS.blue.r + 0.55 * COLORS.paper.r,
    0.45 * COLORS.blue.g + 0.55 * COLORS.paper.g,
    0.45 * COLORS.blue.b + 0.55 * COLORS.paper.b,

3. Scan and Reconstruct

A 120 kVp / 200 mA axial acquisition (360 views, 0.5 s) on the GE Revolution Apex (REVOLUTION_APEX, its Gemstone detector, bowtie and DAS) narrowed to a compact 16-row detector of 512 one-millimetre columns, each view integrated over the arc the gantry turns through while the detector reads it (view_samples = 5, notebook 01), then the standard chain: calibrate_bhc_water → apply_bhc_water → FDK → HU. The function below runs it for either phantom and also returns the largest line integral in the sinogram.

The scan includes the patient's scatter (on by default), from the Geant4 scatter kernels the Apex names, and the DAS's scatter correction. The kernels are made for one scanner's distances, so the scanner is a variant of the Apex at its own 625.6 and 1100 mm, with only the detector's rows and columns changed.

scanner = BS.EICTScanner(
    BS.REVOLUTION_APEX;
    detector_rows = 16,
    detector_cols = 512,
    detector_row_size = 1.0,
    detector_col_size = 1.0,
);

scanner is EICTScanner, from the documented constant REVOLUTION_APEX. Its keywords and their values (units and sources: the constant's docstring, ?BS.REVOLUTION_APEX, and the Scanners page). A variant is the same struct with keywords replaced, EICTScanner(BS.REVOLUTION_APEX; field = value).

scatter_kernels"Revolution Apex"
protocol = BS.CTProtocol(kVp = 120.0, mA = 200.0, views = 360, rotation_time = 0.5);
sim_opts = BS.SimOptions(seed = 42, projector = :dd_fast, view_samples = 5);
recon_opts = BS.ReconOptions(matrix_size = (256, 256, 8), fov_cm = 30.0);
"""
    scan_hu(phantom) -> (; hu, max_line_integral)

`create_workspace` → `simulate!` → water BHC → FDK → HU, returning a CPU volume.
"""
function scan_hu(phantom)
    ws = BS.create_workspace(scanner, protocol, sim_opts, recon_opts, phantom)
    BS.simulate!(ws, phantom, protocol, sim_opts; report_dose = false)
    bhc = BS.calibrate_bhc_water(sim_opts, protocol; scanner, geom = ws.geom)
    sino = BS.apply_bhc_water(ws.sinogram, bhc)
    ws_fdk = BS.create_fdk_recon_workspace(sino, ws.geom, recon_opts.matrix_size)
    μ = BS.reconstruct!(ws_fdk, sino, ws.geom)
    out = (
        hu = Float32.(BS.to_hounsfield(Array(μ); μ_water = bhc.μ_water_ref)),
        max_line_integral = Float64(maximum(ws.sinogram)),
    )
    ws = nothing
    ws_fdk = nothing
    sino = nothing
    μ = nothing
    GC.gc(true)
    return out
end;
scan_ti = scan_hu(phantom);
scan_ref = scan_hu(phantom_reference);

4. The Artifacts

Where They Are Measured

Every number below compares the titanium scan with the metal-free one on the central slice, in three regions: the water between the rods, where beam hardening leaves its dark band; water far from the rods, 8 cm below their axis; and a streak region 3–4.7 cm above the axis, whose spread is the streaks. The profile runs along the rods' axis.

# The measurement regions, as pixel ranges of the central slice (`cn` is the middle pixel)
regions = let
    n = size(scan_ti.hu, 1)
    cn = n ÷ 2
    (
        n = n,
        k = size(scan_ti.hu, 3) ÷ 2,
        dx = recon_opts.fov_cm / n,
        between = ((cn - 8):(cn + 8), (cn - 2):(cn + 2)), # between the rods
        away = ((cn - 8):(cn + 8), (cn - 72):(cn - 64)),  # water, 8 cm below the rod axis
        streaks = (
            (cn - 40):(cn + 40),
            (cn + 30):(cn + 40),
        ), # water band 3–4.7 cm above the axis
        profile_row = cn,
    )
end;
# The mean (or spread) of each region in both scans
artifact = let
    ti = scan_ti.hu[:, :, regions.k]
    ref = scan_ref.hu[:, :, regions.k]
    region_mean(v, r) = Float64(mean(v[r[1], r[2]]))
    region_std(v, r) = Float64(std(v[r[1], r[2]]))
    (
        between = (
            ref = region_mean(ref, regions.between),
            ti = region_mean(ti, regions.between),
        ),
        away = (ref = region_mean(ref, regions.away), ti = region_mean(ti, regions.away)),
        streaks = (
            ref = region_std(ref, regions.streaks),
            ti = region_std(ti, regions.streaks),
        ),
        peak = Float64(maximum(ti)),
    )
end;

The Images

Top: the metal-free reference and the titanium scan in a soft-tissue window. Bottom: the titanium scan in a wide window that shows the rods themselves, and the difference titanium − reference, which is the artifact alone (the anatomy cancels).

MeasurementReference (No Metal)TitaniumTitanium − Reference
between the rods, mean HU0.2-440.7-440.9
water far from the rods, mean HU-0.63.74.3
streak region beside the rods, σ (HU)6.812.4

The water BHC holds the metal-free cylinder at water (-0.6 HU far from the rods). With titanium present, the region between the rods drops by 441 HU: the beam-hardening dark band that a water correction cannot remove. The σ beside the rods rises from 6.8 to 12.4 HU, the streaks. A line integral of 9.1 means the rays through both rods keep about 0.011 % of their unattenuated signal.

5. Scope

  • The water beam-hardening correction is a per-column water polynomial. It is exact for water and leaves the metal artifacts, as measured above. A MAR method (for example sinogram inpainting over the metal trace) would sit on the same reconstruction stack; none ships with the package.

  • Any other implant works the same way: stainless steel, CoCr or amalgam are one XA.Material(...) call each, with NIST XCOM supplying the cross-sections.

Summary

  • A user-defined XA.Material enters the same attenuation pipeline as every built-in tissue.

  • Scanning the same geometry with and without the metal isolates the artifact: the water between the rods reads 441 HU too dark, the spread beside them rises from 6.8 to 12.4 HU, and water far from the rods moves by 4.3 HU.

  • The rays through both rods keep about 0.011 % of their signal, which is where the streaks' noise comes from.

  • :dd_fast, the default projector, keeps its anti-aliased distance-driven footprint in the severe beam hardening around titanium.

  • No MAR claim is made; these numbers are the baseline a future MAR method would be measured against.
